Topics · One God, one message

Why one God, not many gods or a blind force?

Two wills would pull the world apart, the Quran reasons. Then it asks: could a blind force measure and guide?

Part 1 of 4

﴿لَوْ كَانَ فِيهِمَآ ءَالِهَةٌ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُ لَفَسَدَتَا ۚ فَسُبْحَـٰنَ ٱللَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَرْشِ عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Had there been within them [i.e., the heavens and earth] gods besides Allāh, they both would have been ruined. So exalted is Allāh, Lord of the Throne, above what they describe.

Quran · Al-Anbiya 21:22

Translation

“See now that I myself am he. There is no god with me. I kill and I make alive. I wound and I heal. There is no one who can deliver out of my hand.

Original · Hebrew

רְא֣וּ ׀ עַתָּ֗ה כִּ֣י אֲנִ֤י אֲנִי֙ ה֔וּא וְאֵ֥ין אֱלֹהִ֖ים עִמָּדִ֑י אֲנִ֧י אָמִ֣ית וַאֲחַיֶּ֗ה מָחַ֨צְתִּי֙ וַאֲנִ֣י אֶרְפָּ֔א וְאֵ֥ין מִיָּדִ֖י מַצִּֽיל׃

the Torah (Deuteronomy) · 32:39

World English Bible

Imagine two sources of the world, each with a will of its own. So long as the wills are independent, they may agree or differ. At the first difference, whose will goes ahead? If one gives way, the other stands above it, and it is no final source. If neither does, the world is pulled between two. The verse says the order we see, in which the sun rises, grass grows and waves move together, is evidence that the source is one.

A question for you

If two sources of the world each had a will, what would happen at their first disagreement?

If you sayOne would give way
ThenThen the other stands above it, and it is no final source. That is the heart of the argument: a final source has no one above it.
If you sayThey would never differ
ThenThen ask what guarantees it. If something does, that is above them. If each stays free, difference stays possible, and the next verse takes that up.
If you sayThe world would show it
ThenThat is the verse's point: the world's order is the evidence. If you see no quarrel in the world, that is what one source would predict.

Part 2 of 4

﴿مَا ٱتَّخَذَ ٱللَّهُ مِن وَلَدٍ وَمَا كَانَ مَعَهُۥ مِنْ إِلَـٰهٍ ۚ إِذًا لَّذَهَبَ كُلُّ إِلَـٰهٍۭ بِمَا خَلَقَ وَلَعَلَا بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ ۚ سُبْحَـٰنَ ٱللَّهِ عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Allāh has not taken any son, nor has there ever been with Him any deity. [If there had been], then each deity would have taken what it created, and some of them would have [sought to] overcome others. Exalted is Allāh above what they describe [concerning Him].

Quran · Al-Mu'minun 23:91

Translation

Don’t fear, neither be afraid. Haven’t I declared it to you long ago, and shown it? You are my witnesses. Is there a God besides me? Indeed, there is not. I don’t know any other Rock.”

Original · Hebrew

אַֽל־תִּפְחֲדוּ֙ וְאַל־תִּרְה֔וּ הֲלֹ֥א מֵאָ֛ז הִשְׁמַעְתִּ֥יךָ וְהִגַּ֖דְתִּי וְאַתֶּ֣ם עֵדָ֑י הֲיֵ֤שׁ אֱל֨וֹהַּ֙ מִבַּלְעָדַ֔י וְאֵ֥ין צ֖וּר בַּל־יָדָֽעְתִּי׃

Isaiah · 44:8

World English Bible

The verse adds a finer picture of what would have happened: each god would go off with what he created, and some would rise over others. A source that makes something claims it as its own, claiming makes borders, and borders make contests. If they settled things by agreement, either each can break it, and the contest is back, or something holds them to it, and that stands above them. Either way, no true partner remains.

A question for you

If two powers made the world together, what would settle whose word counts at the border between their work?

If you sayAn agreement between them
ThenEither each can break it, and the contest returns, or something holds them to it, and that stands above them both.
If you sayThe stronger of the two
ThenThen the stronger is the one whose word counts, and the other is not what we mean by a source. That is what the verse says: some would rise over others.
If you sayNothing needs to settle it
ThenThen the two would make two worlds that never touch. But a leaf meets the sun and the sea meets the moon; things do touch, and they meet under one law.

Part 3 of 4

﴿قُل لَّوْ كَانَ مَعَهُۥٓ ءَالِهَةٌ كَمَا يَقُولُونَ إِذًا لَّٱبْتَغَوْا۟ إِلَىٰ ذِى ٱلْعَرْشِ سَبِيلًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

Say, [O Muḥammad], "If there had been with Him [other] gods, as they say, then they [each] would have sought to the Owner of the Throne a way."[747]

Translator's notes

[747] To please Him, recognizing His superiority. Another interpretation is "...they would seek a way" to depose Him (subḥānahu wa taʿālā) and take over His Throne.

Quran · Al-Isra 17:42

The verse speaks to those who say there are gods alongside God. It says: if there were other gods with Him, they would seek a way to the Lord of the Throne. Scholars read this two ways. First: they would seek a way to overcome Him and rise over Him. Second: they would seek a way to draw near to Him. On both readings these gods look upward, toward Him, and do not stand at His rank.

A question for you

Which reading do you lean toward: that they would seek to overcome, or that they would seek to draw near?

If you sayTo overcome
ThenThat reading rests on the logic of independent wills competing. The result is that the supposed gods turn toward the Lord of the Throne, even if to contest Him.
If you sayTo draw near
ThenThat reading sees them as servants seeking a place with Him. Their existence then depends on His, and is no parallel source.
If you sayBoth lead to the same place
ThenThen you see what the two share: on either reading, these gods turn toward Him.

Part 4 of 4

﴿بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ سَبِّحِ ٱسْمَ رَبِّكَ ٱلْأَعْلَى١ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ فَسَوَّىٰ٢ وَٱلَّذِى قَدَّرَ فَهَدَىٰ٣﴾

Translation of the meaning

Exalt the name of your Lord, the Most High, Who created and proportioned And who destined and [then] guided

Quran · Al-A'la 87:1-3

Translation

He blessed him, and said, “Blessed be Abram of God Most High, possessor of heaven and earth. Blessed be God Most High, who has delivered your enemies into your hand.” Abram gave him a tenth of all.

Original · Hebrew

וַֽיְבָרְכֵ֖הוּ וַיֹּאמַ֑ר בָּר֤וּךְ אַבְרָם֙ לְאֵ֣ל עֶלְי֔וֹן קֹנֵ֖ה שָׁמַ֥יִם וָאָֽרֶץ׃ וּבָרוּךְ֙ אֵ֣ל עֶלְי֔וֹן אֲשֶׁר־מִגֵּ֥ן צָרֶ֖יךָ בְּיָדֶ֑ךָ וַיִּתֶּן־ל֥וֹ מַעֲשֵׂ֖ר מִכֹּֽל׃

the Torah (Genesis) · 14:19-20

World English Bible

A force is a different question. A force pushes. It does not choose a measure for each thing, give it its nature, and guide it toward what it is for. The verses name four acts: created, shaped, measured, guided. If what stands behind the world measures and guides, it is nearer to a will that knows than to a blind push. So measuring and guiding, as these verses name them, point to a will and not a push.

A question for you

Which of these acts could you ascribe to a blind force?

If you sayPushing and bringing into being
ThenPerhaps. But the verse does not stop at the beginning; it joins beginning and measure.
If you sayMeasuring: giving each thing its measure
ThenThat is harder for a blind force, because a measure assumes an end. The verse calls the measuring an act.
If you sayGuidance: directing each thing to what it is for
ThenThat is harder still, since guidance assumes knowing the destination. This is where a push and a will part.

The same in the other books

Oh clap your hands, all you nations. Shout to God with the voice of triumph! For Yahweh Most High is awesome. He is a great King over all the earth.

It is good to bless God and exalt his name, showing forth with honor the works of God. Don’t be slack to give him thanks.
